rounds.learn: A list holds many values in order, inside square brackets. Every value has a spot number. Counting starts at 0, so the first value is at [0].
rounds.task: Make a list of tools. Print the first one.
rounds.say: hammer. Spot 0 is the first one.

rounds.learn: .append() adds a value to the end of a list. len() tells you how many values the list has.
rounds.task: Add a drill to the end. Print the list, then how long it is.
rounds.say: The drill landed at the end, and len() counted 3.

rounds.task: Add 16 to the end of nums. Print the second number.
rounds.say: 8. Spot 1 is the second number, because counting starts at 0.

rounds.task: Make a list called jobs with two jobs in it. Add a third job with append. Print how many jobs there are.
rounds.say: 3. You built, grew and measured a list.
